instructions:
Below is an essay you revised once. Revise it so that it reads as if a US grade 12 student wrote it in class for a timed writing test. Keep the position it argues and keep it at about 295 words. The file must contain only the revised essay.

Essay:

A lot of students think taking classes from home would be perfect. You don't have to wake up early for the bus, you don't have to push through packed hallways, and you can eat lunch in your own kitchen. I think distance learning can help some students in certain situations, but for most students going to school in person is still better.

First off, distance learning does help students who can't be in a classroom. If someone is recovering from surgery, taking care of a sick parent, or lives really far from school, online classes let them keep up instead of falling behind. For those students it's a big deal, and schools should give them that option.

But for the average student, learning at home has real problems. The biggest one is focus. At home you have your phone, video games, and maybe little brothers or sisters all distracting you, and there's no teacher walking around to notice you zoning out. We saw this during the pandemic. Grades went down and some kids just stopped logging in at all.

Also, school isn't only about the lessons. In class you learn how to work in groups, deal with arguments, and make friends. Talking with people before class or joking around at lunch builds social skills that a Zoom call can't really replace. Clubs, sports, and science labs also need you to actually be there.

Another thing is that not every family has good wifi or a quiet place to study, so online school can make the gap between kids who have stuff and kids who don't even bigger.

In conclusion, distance learning should be there for students who really need it, but most students do better with the structure and the people in a real classroom.
